title: Evaluate PR 4: package-json version mode (commit-time version bump)
description:
PR 4 (branch claude/add-alternate-version-mode-Hnq9X) adds versionMode: "package-json" — a pre-commit hook that computes the next version and writes it into package.json, so the committed package.json always carries the real version. Goal (Justin): get the dynamic-version effect WITHOUT dynamic-version.local.json, which breaks CI (file is gitignored, remote envs must regenerate it) and breaks Expo EAS builds (which historically packed the repo without .git, making generation impossible). Target repos: eslint-config-jha-react-node, prompts — small, linear-history, low-ceremony.

Written ~2026-03 by Claude 4 Opus. Rebased onto main 2026-09-16 as local branch pr-4-package-json-mode (3 commits, one conflict in src/git-hooks-manager.ts resolved by keeping mains nonFatalSuffix and applying it to post-* hooks in both modes, deliberately NOT to pre-commit).
design:
VERDICT: the core idea is sound and worth keeping, but only for linear-history repos, and the implementation needs fixes before it is safe.

=== WHAT WORKS (verified by tests/integration/package-json-mode.test.ts, 16 tests) ===
- Sequential commits increment correctly in both calculation modes.
- Self-healing after --no-verify works exactly as designed: version set i commits ago yields +(i+1).
- The bumped version lands INSIDE the commit; working tree is left clean.
- package.json alone is sufficient for a consumer — no .git, no generated file. This is the goal of the PR and it is met.

=== VERIFIED BY TEST OR PROBE ===
1. npm STRIPS build metadata on publish. Probe: `npm publish --dry-run` on version 1.0.0+5 produced "publishprobe@1.0.0" and filename publishprobe-1.0.0.tgz. So append-commits — the DEFAULT calculation mode — makes every commit publish as the same version; the registry rejects the second. add-to-patch must be the default for this mode. (Closed as not-a-blocker in 70i.1: Justin does not publish to npm.)
2. Unequal-length branches ALWAYS conflict on package.json (test). Equal-length branches are subtler and worse: both sides compute the SAME version, git auto-merges cleanly, and the merged result undercounts (two commits of work, one version) (test). 70i.10 (branch suffix) makes that case a visible conflict.
3. The design-doc claim "on the merge commit the pre-commit hook recalculates" is FALSE (test). git merge fires pre-merge-commit, not pre-commit; auto-merge commits keep a stale version.
4. git commit --amend re-runs pre-commit and double-bumps (test).
5. Rebase never re-runs the hook: the branch gains a commit while the version stands still (test).
6. The hook reads/writes the WORKING TREE package.json then `git add`s the whole file, so an unstaged half-finished package.json edit is silently swept into the commit (test). Data integrity, not just a `git add -p` annoyance. Fixed by 70i.3.
7. updateLockfile() buys nothing. Probes: bun.lock records the root name but NOT the root version (grep: zero "version" keys), and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` after a version-only bump exits 0; package-lock.json DOES record the root version but `npm ci` after a version-only bump also exits 0. `npm version X --no-git-tag-version --offline` updates both files instantly and offline if the drift is ever worth closing. Removed by 70i.5.
8. A failing package manager inside the hook is swallowed: a stub npm that exits 1 (proven invoked via a marker file) leaves the commit succeeding with no signal (test). "Failure is not empty" violation. Fixed by 70i.4.

=== INFERRED FROM CODE READING, NOT DEMONSTRATED ===
9. stageFiles() also catches everything and only console.warn()s. If `git add` itself failed, package.json would be rewritten on disk but never staged, so the commit would record the OLD version while the tree shows the new one. I did not induce a git-add failure; this is a read of src/script-manager.ts, not an observation.
10. installCommand() calls generateVersionFile() (which creates version-manager.json with the default dynamic-file) BEFORE getVersionMode(), and no --mode flag exists — so a first install appears unable to produce package-json hooks; the user must install, hand-edit config, install again. Read from src/index.ts ordering; not executed end-to-end. (70i.7, not in the current push.)
11. installGitHooks() only writes the current mode's hooks and has no removal path, so switching package-json -> dynamic-file appears to leave pre-commit live forever. The leftover-file half IS covered by a test; that the leftover hook keeps bumping on later commits is inferred. (70i.6, not in the current push.)
12. RESERVED_VERSION_NAMES gains "main" with no rationale anywhere in the diff or the plan. Observation, not a defect.

=== STYLE / RULES ===
- docs/plans/2026-03-27_committed-version-modes.md violated the current critical rules (beads replaced docs/plans/). DONE 2026-09-19 (70i.9): deleted in 35987e0; content preserved above.
- calculatePreCommitVersion() duplicates its add-to-patch arithmetic three times.
- preCommitHandler(outputPath: string) is typed string but yargs supplies undefined (--output has no default); the ?? fallback is load-bearing while the type says it cannot fire.

=== CONDUCTOR DECISIONS, 2026-09-19 (binding on every dispatch in this push) ===

D1. SCOPE OF THIS PUSH. 70i.10, then 70i.2, 70i.3, 70i.5+70i.4, then 70i.8 if budget allows. 70i.6 and 70i.7 are explicitly NOT in this push. 70i.9 is done.

D2. BRANCH SUFFIX FORMAT (70i.10). `<core>-<sanitised-branch>.<n>` with the prerelease inserted before any +build metadata. Examples: 0.32.3 -> 0.32.3-feat-x.3; 0.32.1+3 -> 0.32.1-feat-x.3+3. A hyphen prerelease sorts BEFORE the release, which is correct: a branch build is a prerelease of the version it will become.

D3. VERSION-MANAGER OWNS THE PRERELEASE SEGMENT WHEN THE KNOB IS ON. This is the load-bearing decision. In package-json mode the decorated version is COMMITTED into package.json, so the next computation reads it back as its own input — a feedback loop that would otherwise compound (0.1.0-b.1 -> 0.1.0-b.1-b.2). Therefore: every computation strips the entire existing prerelease from the current/base version before calculating, and re-applies a freshly computed suffix at the end. Consequence, accepted and documented: with the knob ON, a hand-authored prerelease in package.json (1.0.0-beta.1) is discarded on the next hooked commit. The knob is off by default; this limitation is documented in the README and pinned by a test. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: a marker token (0.32.1-branch.feat-x.3) that makes the suffix recognisable so hand-authored prereleases survive — rejected because it deviates from the shape Justin wrote down and buys a case he does not have. Revisit only if a real base prerelease appears.

D4. SANITISATION, exact rules. (a) Replace every character outside [0-9A-Za-z-] with '-' (so slashes AND dots in branch names both become '-'; the only dot in the suffix is the one before n). (b) Collapse runs of '-' to one. (c) Trim leading/trailing '-'. (d) Empty result -> the literal 'branch'. (e) All-digits result -> prefix 'b' (semver forbids leading zeros in a numeric identifier; 007 -> b007). Sanitisation is lossy and may collide (feat/x and feat-x both -> feat-x); that is accepted and documented.

D5. WHAT n IS. n = commits on this branch since its merge base with the main branch, measured by `git rev-list --count <mainBranch>..HEAD`, plus 1 in the pre-commit path for the about-to-happen commit. Reason: the count the modes already compute is useless here — in package-json mode the version changes on EVERY commit, so commitsSinceLastChange is always 0 and n would always be 1. If no configured main branch ref resolves, fall back to `git rev-list --count HEAD` (total commits) and say so in verbose output. If BOTH measurements fail, apply NO suffix and return the undecorated version — never substitute 0 for a failed measurement (critical rule 6).

D6. WHICH BRANCHES ARE "MAIN". config.branchSuffix.mainBranches, default ["main", "master"]. On a listed branch, and in detached HEAD (getCurrentBranch returns "HEAD"), no suffix is applied.

D7. n === 0 MEANS NO SUFFIX. A branch with no commits of its own is bit-identical to its base, so it gets the undecorated version. Prevents 0.32.1-my-branch.0 sorting below the release it equals.

D8. THE KNOB APPLIES TO BOTH versionModes. dynamic-file gets it in the generated file (no feedback hazard, base always comes from an undecorated package.json); package-json gets it committed. Same config field, same helper, one code path.

D9. INDEX IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH IN PRE-COMMIT (70i.3). The current version is read from the INDEX (`git show :package.json`), which equals HEAD's content when package.json is unstaged — one rule covers both cases. The new content is written to the index surgically (hash-object + update-index), and the working-tree file gets only its version field rewritten, so unstaged edits elsewhere in package.json survive and are NOT staged.

D10. FAIL LOUDLY IN THE HOOK (70i.4). A failed stage or a failed package-manager call aborts the commit with a non-zero exit and a message naming the exact failed command. A commit that records the wrong version is worse than a blocked commit, and `--no-verify` self-heals by design.

D11. MERGE DRIVER POLICY (70i.8). Justin, 2026-09-19: default to OURS (the branch being merged into, i.e. main) for the version field. The pre-commit hook then adds exactly 1 on top, so a squash of a 500-commit branch lands at main+1.

D12. NO NEW dynamic-version.local.json IN package-json MODE (70i.2). In package-json mode nothing is written unless --output is passed explicitly; the post-* hooks are not installed, and the *.local.json gitignore prompt is skipped. The watcher and the metro plugin still write the file in package-json mode — out of scope here, filed as 70i.11.
acceptance_criteria: Justin has: (a) a clear verdict on whether the approach is worth keeping, (b) verified evidence for each claim rather than inference, (c) a prioritised list of what must change before it is safe to use, (d) automated tests that pin the behaviour so a future fix flips a documented expectation.

title: Branch-name suffix in version when not on main (0.32.1-my-branch.3)
description:
Justin's idea (2026-09-16): when not on the main branch, include the branch name in the computed version, e.g. 0.32.1-my-branch.3.

STATUS 2026-09-19: BUILT AND VERIFIED on branch pr-4-package-json-mode. Commits cadafeb (source), 81de36f (tests), 07dcaa6 (README), 68ed093 (all-digits test). Not closed — awaiting conductor review.

WHAT EXISTS NOW
- src/branch-suffix.ts — pure, no I/O: sanitizeBranchName (D4), stripPrerelease, applyBranchSuffix (D2), isSuffixExemptBranch (D6), decideBranchSuffix (the D5/D6/D7 policy, taking measurements as input so every failure combination is unit-testable).
- src/git-utils.ts — countCommitsSinceRef(ref) and countCommitsOnHead(), both number | null, null on failure, never 0. countCommitsSinceRef refuses a ref outside /^[A-Za-z0-9._\/-]+$/ (it comes from user-authored config and reaches a shell).
- src/types.ts — BranchSuffixConfigSchema exactly as specified: enabled default false, mainBranches default [main, master], the whole object defaulted. Survives an absent field and a partial object; both are pinned by tests.
- src/version-generator.ts — measureBranchCommitCounts() + planBranchSuffix() + decorateVersion(); wired into BOTH generateFileBasedVersion() and generatePreCommitVersionData() (D8). GenerateVersionResult gained branchSuffixWarning: string | null.
- src/script-manager.ts — readPreCommitBaseVersion() / writePreCommitVersion(): the two named helpers 70i.3 swaps to index reads/writes. The suffix logic is not inlined into either.
- src/index.ts — preCommitHandler uses writePreCommitVersion; both handlers console.warn the branchSuffixWarning when the format is not silent.
- README.md — "Branch Name Suffix (opt-in)" section: format, n, sanitisation, precedence, and the D3 limitation.

D3 IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART. While the knob is on, the prerelease is stripped before either calculate function sees the version and a fresh suffix is applied after. Proven necessary, not assumed: with the strip removed, add-to-patch went 0.1.1-feat-x.1 -> 0.1.1-feat-x.2 -> 0.1.1-feat-x.3 — the CORE FROZE at 0.1.1 while only n advanced, silently, exit code 0.

SEMANTIC CONTRACTS (unchanged from the spec, all pinned by tests)
- Format <core>-<sanitised-branch>.<n>, prerelease before any +build metadata.
- n = commits since the merge base with the first main branch that resolves, +1 in pre-commit.
- Configured main branches and detached HEAD get no suffix.
- n === 0 gets no suffix.
- A failed measurement yields the UNDECORATED version, never n = 0 or n = 1.

OUT OF SCOPE AND UNTOUCHED: the merge driver (70i.8), the --mode flag (70i.7), stale-hook removal (70i.6), dropping dynamic-version.local.json writes (70i.2), the watcher/metro plugin (70i.11). The watcher and metro plugin DO inherit the knob, because they call generateFileBasedVersion; that is the shared-code-path consequence the spec allowed.
design:
DESIGN DECISIONS ARE IN THE EPIC (version-manager-70i) design field, items D2 through D8. Read them before starting; they are binding. Summary:
- Format <core>-<sanitised-branch>.<n>, prerelease inserted before any +build metadata (D2).
- version-manager OWNS the prerelease segment while the knob is on; strip before calculating, re-apply after (D3). This is the decision that prevents the feedback loop.
- Exact sanitisation rules (D4).
- n = commits since the merge base with the main branch, +1 in pre-commit; fallbacks and the no-measurement case (D5).
- mainBranches config, detached HEAD excluded (D6).
- n === 0 means no suffix (D7).
- Applies to both versionModes through one code path (D8).
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. `bun run signal` clean, and `bun test` showing no failure that main does not also have (measured baseline is recorded in the epic notes). Run the suite with npm_config_cache redirected into $TMPDIR or the install tests EPERM. New tests in this file get an explicit per-test timeout (>= 20000ms); the default 5s timeout makes package-json-mode tests flake under full-suite load.

BEHAVIOUR (each item needs a test)
1. Off by default. A config with no branchSuffix field, and a repo with no version-manager.json at all, both produce today's undecorated versions in both versionModes.
2. Sanitisation: branch "claude/add-alternate-version-mode-Hnq9X" produces a valid semver; so do branch names containing dots, spaces, and consecutive separators. Assert validity with semver.valid() from the `semver` package added as a DEV dependency only (runtime dep count stays where CLAUDE.md wants it), not with a hand-rolled regex.
3. Sanitisation edge cases: an all-punctuation branch name yields the literal "branch"; an all-digits branch name is prefixed with "b" (leading zeros are illegal in a semver numeric identifier).
4. main is untouched: on "main" and on "master" the version is undecorated with the knob ON. Detached HEAD (getCurrentBranch() returns "HEAD") is also undecorated.
5. n === 0 yields no suffix.
6. Equal-length branches no longer collide: the existing package-json-mode test that shows two equal-length branches auto-merging to the same undercounted version stays as the knob-OFF control, and a knob-ON twin shows the two sides producing DIFFERENT versions so the merge conflicts visibly instead of silently undercounting.
7. No feedback loop in package-json mode: with the knob on, successive commits on a branch go 0.1.1-feat-x.1 -> 0.1.2-feat-x.2 (add-to-patch) rather than compounding suffixes or freezing. Cover append-commits too: the prerelease sits before the +N metadata.
8. Both versionModes: dynamic-file writes the decorated version into dynamic-version.local.json; package-json commits it into package.json.
9. Failure is not empty: when the configured main branches do not resolve, the count falls back to the total commit count and the version is still produced; when no count can be measured at all, the UNDECORATED version is returned. No path may substitute 0 for a failed measurement.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS (required, and reported)
For at least the sanitisation test, the main-untouched test, and the feedback-loop test: break the implementation, watch the test fail, restore it, and report what the failure message was. An unproven test is no test.
notes:
GATE, measured 2026-09-19 on pr-4-package-json-mode at 68ed093.
- bun run signal: FULLY GREEN (ts-check, eslint, prettier).
- Full suite (TMPDIR=... npm_config_cache="$TMPDIR/npm-cache" bun test): 208 pass / 1 skip / 8 fail. The failing SET is byte-identical to the recorded baseline (2 compact-mode snapshots, 5 Watch Command, 1 husky bun.lock). NO ninth failure. Branch went 122 -> 208 passing, i.e. 86 new tests.
- New tests: 63 unit (tests/unit/branch-suffix.test.ts), 18 integration (tests/integration/branch-suffix.test.ts), 5 integration added to tests/integration/package-json-mode.test.ts. Every new integration test carries an explicit 30000ms timeout.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN (break it, watch it fail, restore it)
1. Sanitisation — removed the character-class replace in sanitizeBranchName. 24 of 63 unit tests failed, e.g. Expected "claude-add-alternate-version-mode-Hnq9X" / Received "claude/add-alternate-version-mode-Hnq9X"; the semver-validity assertions failed with Received: null. Integration: Expected "0.32.2-claude-add-alternate-version-mode-Hnq9X.1" / Received "0.32.2-claude/add-alternate-version-mode-Hnq9X.1". Restored: 63/63 and 18/18.
2. Main-untouched — made isSuffixExemptBranch always return false. All three AC-4 tests failed: "0.1.2" vs "0.1.2-master.2", "0.1.2" vs "0.1.2-main.2", "0.1.2" vs "0.1.2-HEAD.2". The sibling control ("a non-main branch IS decorated") kept passing, so the three are not passing via D7. Restored: green.
3. Feedback loop — removed the D3 strip in generatePreCommitVersionData. add-to-patch produced ["0.1.1-feat-x.1", "0.1.1-feat-x.2", "0.1.1-feat-x.3"] instead of 0.1.1/0.1.2/0.1.3 — THE CORE FROZE, exit code 0, no error. The land-on-main test gave Expected "0.1.2" / Received "0.1.1-feat-x.1", frozen forever. Restored: green.
   NOTE from control 3: the append-commits path did NOT fail, because applyBranchSuffix strips internally and masked the missing strip. Only add-to-patch exposes it. So the defensive strip inside applyBranchSuffix is load-bearing for coverage, not decoration.

MEASUREMENTS MADE THIS SESSION
- git init.defaultBranch is "main" globally, so fixtures start on main; tests assert the base branch is main or master rather than assuming.
- semver.valid() returns the NORMALISED version, which DROPS build metadata. So valid("0.32.1-x.3+7") === "0.32.1-x.3". Assertions on +N cases check parseability plus the emitted string separately.
- In package-json mode commitsSinceLastChange is always 0, as the epic states (confirmed by the observed 1-per-commit increments).
- bun add EPERMs in the sandbox unless TMPDIR is pointed at a writable dir: TMPDIR=/tmp/claude-501/bun-tmp BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=... bun add -d ... works.

DEVIATIONS FROM SPEC (all reported to the conductor)
D1. The git counting helper is TWO functions (countCommitsSinceRef, countCommitsOnHead), each number | null as specified, rather than one; the main-branch fallback loop lives in version-generator.measureBranchCommitCounts(). Reason: the spec also requires the fallback chain to be testable, and a pure decision function taking grouped measurements makes the "both measurements failed" branch unit-testable, which no integration fixture can reach.
D2. Integration tests live in a NEW file tests/integration/branch-suffix.test.ts, not only in package-json-mode.test.ts. Reason: the knob spans both version modes and that file is scoped to one. The AC-6 knob-ON twin IS in package-json-mode.test.ts, directly beneath the knob-OFF control it twins, as specified.
D3. @types/semver was added as a devDependency alongside semver. semver 7 ships no types and ts-check would fail without it. Neither is a runtime dependency.
D4. VersionManagerConfig now has branchSuffix as a REQUIRED output field (the schema default makes it so), which means any config version-manager REWRITES — a legacy migration, or a bump that updates custom versions — will now gain a branchSuffix block on disk. Configs that are merely read are untouched (the "does not modify new format config" test still passes). This falls out of the exact schema shape the epic specified; flagging it because it is user-visible.
D5. applyBranchSuffix() strips any existing prerelease internally, making it idempotent, and returns the undecorated version for n <= 0 or a non-integer n. The spec described it only as "inserts after the version core"; the guards are defensive.

NOT VERIFIED / KNOWN GAPS
- "No count can be measured at all" (AC 9, second half) is proven by UNIT test on decideBranchSuffix, not end to end. A repo where both git rev-list calls fail is a repo with no commits, and generateFileBasedVersion throws earlier at getGitDescribe, so no integration fixture can reach that branch.
- The all-punctuation branch name (AC 3) is unit-only: git will not create a branch whose name sanitises to nothing.
- The warning text is asserted end to end via "2>&1" appended to the CLI command, because TestRepo.runCli cannot return stderr on a SUCCESSFUL run (execSync returns stdout only). Left alone rather than rewriting a shared helper.
- The knob was deliberately NOT enabled in this repo own version-manager.json.

Negative controls were run and their failure messages reported; control 3 showed the version core freezing at 0.1.1 with exit code 0, demonstrating the silent-freeze landmine rather than assuming it. Three interpretations of D3/D5 APPROVED as built. Two minor findings carried to the fix round in the findings bead, neither blocking. One out-of-scope change (an unrelated justin-sdk pin bump) was reverted by the conductor in a separate commit.

title: Watcher and metro plugin still write dynamic-version.local.json in package-json mode
description:
70i.2 stops the CLI and the git hooks from writing dynamic-version.local.json in package-json mode. src/watcher.ts and src/metro-plugin.ts were deliberately left out of that change and still write the file on every trigger, which reopens exactly the hole package-json mode exists to close.

FIX SHAPE: both call into the same generate path; make them respect the same mode decision 70i.2 centralises. A watcher running in package-json mode has nothing useful to write, so it should either no-op with one clear message at startup or refuse to start.
acceptance_criteria: A watcher run and a metro bundle in package-json mode both leave no dynamic-version.local.json, proven by a test. dynamic-file behaviour unchanged.

title: README documents nothing about package-json mode
description:
DONE 2026-09-19 in commit 120b91a on pr-4-package-json-mode. The README had ZERO hits for versionMode or package-json before this; it now documents the mode end to end.

WHAT LANDED: a section "Version Modes: where the computed version ends up", placed between the calculation modes and the branch suffix, containing:
- A comparison table of the two modes: where the version lands, when it is computed, what a consumer needs, what history each tolerates.
- Why package-json mode exists, naming the two failures it was built for (a gitignored file has to be regenerated wherever the code is built: CI needs .git and the history; Expo EAS has historically packed the repo without .git) and what it costs.
- How to turn it on, with the config to write, and the honest part: there is no --mode flag and install does not ask, so version-manager.json has to exist and say package-json BEFORE the install (70i.7). Measured, not inferred: install --help lists no mode option, and an install in a repo with no config creates nothing and asks nothing.
- What install writes in that mode (pre-commit hook, no post-* hooks, no lifecycle scripts, no gitignore entries, no generated file unless --output is explicit).
- What switching an existing project over leaves behind — post-* hooks that keep running, a generated file that goes stale, lifecycle scripts — with the warning not to delete a hook file without reading it, since install appends to hooks that already exist (70i.6, 70i.15).
- What the pre-commit hook does exactly: index as the source of truth, unstaged edits not swept in, fails loudly, no package manager, --no-verify self-heals.
- Known limitations: amend double-bumps, rebase never re-runs the hook, an auto-merge commit keeps a stale version (git fires pre-merge-commit, not pre-commit), and the equal-length/unequal-length branch pair. Each names the test that pins it. Two more are marked "(probe, not a test)": npm strips +N on publish, and a GitHub install today runs a dist/ from 2026-06-11 that has none of this (70i.20).

THE MERGE DRIVER SECTION was extended in the same commit: the 70i.24 knob (off by default, both conditions required, and the reason), a measured bullet that the stale dist cannot run the driver at all — `node dist/index.js merge-driver` answers `Unknown arguments: merge-driver` and exits 1 without merging, which is exactly the 70i.22 trap — and a bullet that nothing takes the registration back (70i.23).

THE BRANCHSUFFIX KNOB and the merge driver's ours policy are documented in their own existing sections (format, default, sanitisation, the prerelease-ownership limitation; the ours policy and the GitHub-button answer). The new section cross-links them rather than restating them, deliberately: two copies of the same behaviour is how documentation drifts.

DEVIATIONS, both called out in the commit message. Two corrections outside this bead's scope, made because the new section would otherwise contradict them in the same file: the version-manager.json example showed the legacy top-level runtimeVersion shape, and the Installation list claimed install creates version-manager.json (measured: it does not).

title: Fix round: conductor review findings for the 70i push
description:
Running list of findings from conductor review between dispatches. Each is numbered, carries its fix shape, and is dispositioned when fixed. None blocked the dispatch that followed it.

F1 (from 70i.10, minor, OPEN). countCommitsSinceRef() in src/git-utils.ts returns null for THREE different reasons — the ref failed SAFE_REF_PATTERN, the ref did not resolve, or git errored — and the caller's warning then says 'none of the configured main branches resolved', which misattributes the first case. A user who writes a ref with an unusual character is sent looking in the wrong place.
FIX SHAPE: return a discriminated result, or lift the rejected-shape check to the caller, so the warning can name the actual cause. Keep null meaning 'no measurement' at the decision boundary.
RELATED: version-manager-70i.18 collects four more helpers of the same shape in the same file, found while hardening the pre-commit path. Fix them together.

F2 (from 70i.10, minor, OPEN). TestRepo.runCli() uses execSync and cannot return stderr on a SUCCESSFUL run, which forced the branch-suffix warning test to append '2>&1' to the command string. A harness hack inside a test that asserts user-facing text.
FIX SHAPE: switch runCli to spawnSync returning {stdout, stderr, exitCode}, then drop the 2>&1. Shared by every integration test, so change it deliberately and run the whole suite.

F3 (from 70i.10, ACCEPTED, not a defect). branchSuffix carries a zod .default(), so it is a required field on the PARSED config and any version-manager.json that version-manager rewrites gains a branchSuffix block. Configs only read are untouched, and a test pins that. Consequence of the schema shape the conductor specified; it makes the knob discoverable. No action unless Justin dislikes it.

F4 (from 70i.2, FIXED in 0ef1f60 by the 70i.3 dispatch). bumpCommand announced 'Regenerating dynamic-version.local.json...' before a call that writes nothing in package-json mode. Now branched on the same shouldWriteGeneratedFiles decision, with the dynamic-file wording unchanged and pinned by a control test.

F5 (from 70i.2, upgrade hazard, OPEN, OUT OF THIS PUSH). New installs no longer write post-checkout / post-merge / post-rewrite in package-json mode, but an EXISTING install keeps the three it already has, and each now runs the CLI on every checkout to write nothing. That is 70i.6 (stale-hook removal), deliberately out of this push. Recorded so the gap is visible at merge time rather than found by a user.

F6 (from 70i.3, FIXED by the conductor). The bunfig preload raising the default test timeout did not reliably reach a full-suite run: three consecutive runs of one unchanged tree gave 10, 8, 8 failures, the extras dying at exactly 5000ms. --timeout 30000 now lives on the test script, which nothing can be scoped away from; the preload stays as a backstop for a bare bun test. Two consecutive runs after the fix: 243 pass / 1 skip / 8 fail.

F7 (from 70i.3, FIXED 2026-09-19 by the 70i.5+70i.4 dispatch). writePreCommitVersion() wrote the output of the hand-rolled scanner in src/json-text-edit.ts straight to the index and the working tree with no post-condition check, so a future bug in it would corrupt package.json SILENTLY.
WHAT LANDED: assertVersionReplaced() in src/script-manager.ts, called on BOTH replacements before either is written. When the input parsed as JSON, the output must parse too and its top-level version must equal the value intended; otherwise it throws, naming the file, and nothing is written. The check is deliberately skipped when the INPUT did not parse — a half-finished working-tree package.json is the author's own file, and blocking a commit over it is not this hook's job. In practice that tolerant branch only ever applies to the working tree, since readPreCommitBaseVersion() already throws on an unparseable index copy.
IT CATCHES A REAL DISAGREEMENT, NOT A HYPOTHETICAL ONE. A package.json with two top-level version keys is valid JSON whose value is the LAST one, while the scanner replaces the FIRST. Measured with the guard removed: the hook writes 9.9.10 into the first key, the commit SUCCEEDS with exit 0, and the effective committed version is still 9.9.9 — frozen at that value on every later commit too, with nothing red anywhere. Pinned by tests/unit/version-replacement-guard.test.ts (5 tests) and by 'a replacement that did not take aborts the commit (F7)' in tests/integration/package-json-mode.test.ts, whose negative control is the measurement above.

F8 (from 70i.3, ARCHITECTURAL, Justin's call, conductor default = keep as built). src/json-text-edit.ts is a hand-rolled JSON scanner. jsonc-parser (Microsoft, zero-dependency, what VS Code uses) has modify()/applyEdits() that do exactly this. Critical rule 2 says prefer a mature library; the repo's own README and CLAUDE.md make a documented design decision of having only three runtime dependencies, for install speed and supply-chain surface in consumer projects. Conductor decision: KEEP the hand-rolled version, because the scope is narrow (one top-level string value), it is covered by 13 unit tests, F7 will make a silent failure impossible, and the alternative is a fourth runtime dependency on a path used only by a git hook. The module deletes cleanly if Justin would rather have the library.
NOTE, now that F7 is built: the duplicate-key case F7 caught is a genuine scanner-vs-JSON disagreement rather than a coding slip, and jsonc-parser would have the same ambiguity to resolve. F7's guard is what makes either choice safe, so it does not move this decision.
acceptance_criteria: Every numbered finding is either fixed with a test, or explicitly dispositioned in this bead as accepted-with-reason. `bun run signal` clean and no failure main does not also have.
notes:
F9 (from 70i.4). FIXED 2026-09-19 in 4909064. The .fail() handler routed BOTH failure kinds through failureExitCode(), so `version-manager --no-fail --bogus-flag` exited 0 — a usage error reported as success because a runtime-failure flag was present. The usage/validation branch (err === null) now exits 1 unconditionally; failureExitCode() stays on the command-failure branch, where --no-fail actually means something. Three tests in tests/integration/cli-output.test.ts: unknown flag with --no-fail, unknown flag without it, and a control that a valid --no-fail run still exits 0. Negative control: restoring the old call makes the first fail with Expected: 1, Received: 0.

F1 (from 70i.10). FIXED 2026-09-19 in 23142ef. countCommitsSinceRef() returned a bare null for three facts and the caller blamed all three on resolution. It now returns a discriminated RefCommitCount: counted / rejected-name / unresolved / git-failed(detail). Resolution is its own step — `git rev-parse --verify --quiet <ref>^{commit}` exits 1 for an unknown ref and 128 when git fails (measured) — and the counting is argv-based rather than shell-based so an exit code is available. Null still means "no measurement" at the decision boundary: BranchCommitCounts keeps mergeBase nullable and gains mergeBaseFailures, which the warning reads to name each cause. 5 unit tests on countCommitsSinceRef (including that a real 0 stays a 0), 6 on the warning wording, 1 integration test. Negative control: mapping rejected-name back to unresolved reproduces the exact old wording, "(main branch: no such ref in this repository)". SAFE_REF_PATTERN kept; its comment now says what it is for with argv (whitespace and leading dashes reaching gits option parser, not shell metacharacters). 70i.18 collects four more helpers of the same shape in the same file and is NOT done.

F2 (from 70i.10). FIXED 2026-09-19 in fe4b8bc. TestRepo.runCli() now uses spawnSync (shell: true, keeping the command-string calling convention) and returns stdout, stderr and the exit code for every run; a spawn failure or a death by signal throws instead of being reported as an exit code. All three `2>&1` hacks are gone and the tests assert against stderr specifically; the --silent test additionally asserts stderr is quiet, which the merged-stream version could not distinguish. Shared by every integration test: full suite unchanged at the same 8 pre-existing failures.

F3, F5, F8 unchanged (accepted / out of push). F4, F6, F7 remain fixed.

REMAINING OPEN IN THIS BEAD: none. F1, F2 and F9 were the last three.
close_reason: All nine findings dispositioned. F4, F6, F7, F9, F1 and F2 fixed and verified; F3, F5 and F8 accepted with reasons recorded. F8 (hand-rolled JSON scanner versus jsonc-parser) is the one left as a standing question for Justin, with the conductor default being to keep the hand-rolled module now that F7 makes a silent corruption impossible.

title: install --silent adds no package.json scripts
description:
installCommand() in src/index.ts puts the ENTIRE script-installation block inside `if (!silent)`, together with the console output it was presumably meant to guard. So `version-manager install --silent` installs git hooks and then adds none of the dynamic-version scripts (dynamic-version, :install, :install-scripts, :generate, plus prepare/prebuild/predev/prestart in dynamic-file mode), without saying so.

VERIFIED 2026-09-19 by probe, not inferred: a temp repo in dynamic-file mode with husky pre-declared, run with `install --silent --non-interactive`, came out with hooks installed and package.json carrying no scripts key at all.

Pre-existing on main and unrelated to version-manager-70i.2, which only ran into it because its install tests had to drop --silent in order to observe the scripts at all.

FIX SHAPE: hoist the script installation out of the `if (!silent)` block and leave only its console.log() calls inside.
acceptance_criteria: `install --silent` adds the same scripts a non-silent install adds, and prints nothing — proven by a test asserting both the scripts in package.json and empty stdout. Non-silent install behaviour unchanged.

title: A pre-70i.2 dynamic-version.local.json is left behind and goes stale
description:
version-manager-70i.2 stops package-json mode from WRITING dynamic-version.local.json, but nothing removes one that an earlier version already wrote. A repo that upgrades keeps the old file on disk, and from then on it is never updated: anything importing it reads a version frozen at the moment of the upgrade, with no signal that it has stopped tracking.

That is worse than the file being absent — absent fails loudly at the import, stale reads as current.

Deliberately NOT fixed in 70i.2: deleting a user's file is not something that change should do unasked. Sibling of version-manager-70i.6 (remove stale HOOKS when versionMode changes); both are "clean up what an earlier install left behind" and could land together.

FIX SHAPE: on `install` in package-json mode, detect an existing generated file and either delete it after saying so, or refuse to touch it and print a one-line warning naming the path. Do not delete silently.
acceptance_criteria: After upgrading a package-json-mode repo that already has a dynamic-version.local.json, the user is told about the stale file (or it is removed with an explicit message), proven by a test. Nothing is deleted silently, and dynamic-file mode is unaffected.

title: Integration suite flakes under load: no default test timeout
description:
Most integration tests carry no explicit per-test timeout, so they run against bun's default 5s. Under full-suite load the hook-driven tests — which shell out to git, husky and a package manager — routinely cross 5s and are reported as FAILURES, with no way to tell them apart from real ones except by reading the timings.

MEASURED 2026-09-19 on pr-4-package-json-mode at 3eecf5c, same commit, three consecutive full-suite runs:
- 8 fail / 96s (the known baseline set)
- 16 fail / 221s — the 8, plus 8 tests in package-json-mode.test.ts and git-hooks.test.ts, EVERY extra one landing between 5008ms and 5659ms
- 9 fail / 146s — the 8, plus "each commit bumps the patch version by one" at 5012.90ms
Run alone, package-json-mode.test.ts and git-hooks.test.ts together give 38 pass / 1 fail, and that one failure is the known pre-existing husky bun.lock test.

Why it matters beyond noise: the gate for every dispatch in this push is "the failing set is the known 8, and any extra failure is yours". A load-dependent extra failure spends a reviewer's attention proving a negative, and the next real regression will look exactly like the flake everyone has learned to wave through.

The workaround so far is per-test `, 30000)` on new tests, which only protects tests somebody remembered to annotate.

FIX SHAPE: set the default once for the whole suite rather than per test — `setDefaultTimeout()` from bun:test in a preload module, or `--timeout` in the test script (verify which the installed bun supports before relying on it). Then drop the scattered per-test 30000s as they become redundant. No assertion changes.
acceptance_criteria: Three consecutive full-suite runs on an unchanged tree produce the same failing set, with no failure landing within 100ms of a timeout wall. The per-test 30000ms annotations added during the 70i push are removed where the global default covers them.
close_reason: Fixed by the conductor in the commit that adds bunfig.toml and tests/setup.ts: setDefaultTimeout(30000) via a bun test preload, so it applies however bun test is invoked. Verified by two consecutive full runs landing on 223 pass / 1 skip / 8 fail with the identical failing set, where four earlier runs of an unchanged tree had given 8, 9, 10 and 16.

title: Partial commits leave the real index holding a stale version
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-19 during the 70i.3 dispatch, in a hand-built fixture. PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by 70i.3 — the same probe run against the pre-change tree (0ef1f60) showed the identical staleness.

A partial commit (git commit -m x -- some-file.txt, and likewise git commit -o) runs the pre-commit hook against a TEMPORARY index, not the real one. Everything the hook writes with git update-index (or git add) therefore lands in the temp index, which is what becomes the commit. THE COMMIT IS CORRECT. But the real index is never updated, so afterwards:

  HEAD:         version 0.1.2
  real index:   version 0.1.1   <- stale, one behind
  working tree: version 0.1.2 plus whatever was unstaged

git status then shows "MM package.json", and git diff --cached shows a staged REVERT of the version. The next hooked commit computes from the stale index value and can repeat a version number.

Deliberately not fixed in 70i.3, whose scope was the data-integrity bug (unstaged content reaching history). With 70i.3 in place the partial-commit COMMIT content is now correct — the unstaged edit stays out — which is a strict improvement: before it, the unstaged edit landed in HEAD in this case too (measured).

FIX SHAPE (unproven, think before building): after the surgical write, detect that GIT_INDEX_FILE is set and differs from GIT_DIR/index, and mirror the same blob into the real index too. Verify FIRST that writing the real index mid-commit does not disturb git's own bookkeeping — an untested guess here is worse than the stale entry. The honest alternative is to document partial commits as a known limitation of package-json mode alongside amend and rebase (70i.8).
acceptance_criteria: Either: a test proves that after a partial commit (git commit -m x -- other-file), HEAD, the real index and the working tree all agree on the version, with an unstaged package.json edit still unstaged and still absent from the commit; or the limitation is documented in the README beside the amend/rebase limitations and this bead is closed as wont-fix with that reasoning recorded in it.

title: Shared git-utils/config helpers still conflate failure with a real value
description:
FOUND WHILE HARDENING THE PRE-COMMIT PATH (70i.4 acceptance item 4, which asks for every swallow-and-continue in that path to be listed and dispositioned). These four are in the pre-commit path but are SHARED with the dynamic-file path, so fixing them was deliberately left out of 70i.4 rather than widening that diff into the whole codebase - critical rule 6 violations all the same.

S1. countCommitsBetween() returns 0 when git fails (src/git-utils.ts). "Could not count" arrives as "zero commits". In the pre-commit path it supplies commitsSinceLastChange, so a git failure computes base+1 instead of base+N+1. Under-counts rather than over-counts, and the next successful hooked commit self-heals, which is why it is P2 and not P1.

S2. findLastCommitWhereFieldChanged() catches everything and returns null (src/git-utils.ts). Null means BOTH "the field never changed" and "git failed", and the caller maps null to 0 commits. Same conflation as S1, arriving one layer earlier.

S3. getCurrentBranch() returns the string "HEAD" when git fails (src/git-utils.ts). That is also the real answer for a detached HEAD, and D6 gives detached HEAD no branch suffix - so a FAILED branch measurement silently suppresses the suffix instead of reporting that it could not be taken.

S4. readVersionManagerConfig() console.warns and returns {config: null} for a corrupt or schema-invalid version-manager.json, and getVersionMode() then returns the DEFAULT "dynamic-file" (src/version-generator.ts). In package-json mode that means a typo in the config silently downgrades the mode: the pre-commit hook still runs, but writeGeneratedFiles starts producing dynamic-version.local.json again and the calculation mode reverts to the default. The warning makes it not-silent, but the fallback still points in the reassuring direction.

S5 (smaller, same file family). readPackageJson() console.errors and returns null on a parse failure, so readPreCommitBaseVersion()"s working-tree fallback reports a CORRUPT package.json as "No version found in package.json. Please add a version field" - the wrong instruction for the actual problem.

NOT IN THIS LIST, because they always end in a loud failure anyway: isGitRepository() returning false on any error (the caller throws "Not a git repository"), and hasUncommittedChanges() returning false on error (not used by the pre-commit path - dirty comes from getGitDescribe).

RELATED: 70i.13 F1 is the same shape in countCommitsSinceRef(), already tracked there.
design:
FIX SHAPE, per critical rule 6.2: the failed state becomes a distinct type member the compiler forces callers to handle - number | null for the counts, a discriminated result where the reason matters (S3, S4), never a sentinel that is also a legal value.

- S1/S2: return number | null and string | null respectively, and make the caller decide what an unmeasurable count means. It must NOT silently become 0. countCommitsSinceRef() and countCommitsOnHead() in the same file already do exactly this and are the pattern to copy.
- S3: return null when the measurement failed, and keep "HEAD" strictly for a real detached HEAD. The branch-suffix planner already handles a failed measurement (D5: apply no suffix and say so), so it needs the distinction to reach it.
- S4: distinguish "no config file" (legitimately the defaults) from "there is a config file and it is broken". The second must not resolve to the default versionMode - in package-json mode that silently changes what the tool does. Consider making a broken config fatal in the pre-commit path specifically, where the mode decision is load-bearing.
- S5: let a parse failure propagate as a parse failure so the message names the real problem.

BLAST RADIUS, why this is its own bead: every one of these is on the dynamic-file path too, which is the mode every existing consumer uses. The change is mechanical but wide, and it wants its own test pass rather than riding along inside a pre-commit hardening commit.
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. bun run signal clean. bun test with no failure main does not also have (baseline in the epic notes); npm_config_cache redirected into $TMPDIR; new integration tests carry a per-test timeout of at least 20000ms.

1. Each of S1-S5 either returns a type whose failure member is distinct from every legal success value, or is explicitly dispositioned in this bead as accepted-with-reason.
2. Every caller of a changed signature handles the failure member explicitly; none maps it back onto 0, "", [] or a default.
3. A test per item induces the failure for real (a stub git via GIT_EXEC_PATH works - see stubFailingGit() in tests/integration/package-json-mode.test.ts, and note that a stub merely first on PATH is shadowed by git prepending its exec-path) and asserts the caller reports "unknown", not a fabricated value.
4. The dynamic-file path is regression-tested, since that is what every existing consumer uses.

title: Pre-commit hook reads package.json out of the index twice
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-19, not estimated. A stub git installed via GIT_EXEC_PATH logged every git invocation one hooked commit makes. Thirteen, in order:

  rev-parse --git-dir
  rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
  describe --always --tags --dirty
  ls-files --full-name --stage -- package.json     <- read 1
  cat-file blob <oid>                              <- read 1
  log --format=%H -- package.json
  show HEAD:package.json
  show <commit>:package.json
  rev-list --count <commit>..HEAD
  ls-files --full-name --stage -- package.json     <- read 2, identical
  cat-file blob <oid>                              <- read 2, identical
  hash-object -w --stdin
  update-index --cacheinfo ...

Reads 1 and 2 are the same two commands with the same arguments, microseconds apart: readPreCommitBaseVersion() takes the first to find the base version, and writePreCommitVersion() takes the second to get the content to rewrite. Nothing can have changed in between.

CONTEXT: 70i.5 removed the npm install / bun install the hook used to run on every commit, which cost far more than all thirteen of these together. This is a tidy-up, not a performance problem — hence P4.
design:
FIX SHAPE: thread the GitIndexEntry that readPreCommitBaseVersion() already read through to writePreCommitVersion() instead of re-reading it, e.g. by having readPreCommitBaseVersion() return the entry alongside the version and having generatePreCommitVersionData() hand it to the caller.

WATCH OUT FOR TWO THINGS.
1. The two reads currently sit either side of the whole version calculation. Passing the first entry forward makes the write depend on a value measured earlier, which is FINE in a pre-commit hook (nothing else is touching the index) but should be stated in a comment so nobody later assumes it is a fresh read.
2. readPreCommitBaseVersion() has a documented fallback (D9) for package.json absent from the index, where there is no entry to pass. The threaded value therefore has to carry "there was no index entry" distinctly from "I did not look" - the same rule 6 care the rest of this path now takes.

NOT WORTH DOING ON ITS OWN. Fold it into the next change that touches these two functions.
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. bun run signal clean. bun test with no failure main does not also have.

1. A hooked commit makes ONE ls-files + cat-file pair for package.json, not two. Measurable with the stubFailingGit() pattern in tests/integration/package-json-mode.test.ts, pointed at a logging stub rather than a failing one.
2. The D9 working-tree fallback still works and still warns.
3. No behaviour change otherwise: the existing package-json-mode tests pass unmodified.

title: Stop writing dynamic-version.local.json in package-json mode
description:
THE POINT OF THE WHOLE PR, AND IT IS BUILT. Justin's goal for package-json mode: the dynamic-version effect WITHOUT dynamic-version.local.json, because that file is gitignored — CI must regenerate it (which needs .git) and Expo EAS builds historically packed the repo without .git. PR 4 added the commit-time bump but left every generated-file path in place, so the mode did both. This bead removed the second half.

WHAT LANDED (branch pr-4-package-json-mode)
- 5af80ec feat: the behaviour change.
- f66f6a6 test: the tests.
- 3eecf5c fix: an empty --output counts as absent (see notes).
- decdfaf docs: doc-comment correction.

THE DESIGN. src/generated-file-policy.ts is the single place that decides whether anything is written. Both the CLI path (generateVersionFile) and the hook path (preCommitHandler) in src/index.ts call writeGeneratedFiles(), so the two cannot drift apart. The rule: dynamic-file mode always writes; package-json mode writes only when --output was passed explicitly.

HOW EXPLICITNESS IS KNOWN. The --output option no longer declares a yargs default; resolveOutputPathOption() applies DEFAULT_OUTPUT_PATH and records explicit true/false. Provenance cannot be recovered by comparing the value against the default string — "--output ./dynamic-version.local.json" and no flag at all produce the same string — so the yargs default was removed rather than compared against. defaultDescription keeps --help showing the default (the only visible difference: the path is no longer quoted in the help line).

WHAT ELSE STOPPED IN package-json MODE
- No post-checkout / post-merge / post-rewrite hooks. Their only job was regenerating the file. (post-commit was already absent: pre-commit covers the commit.) PACKAGE_JSON_MODE_POST_HOOKS is deleted from src/git-hooks-manager.ts.
- No prepare/prebuild/predev/prestart lifecycle scripts: addScriptsToPackageJson()'s existing includeLifecycleScripts parameter is now driven by the mode. The bead named prebuild/predev/prestart; "prepare" is in the same LIFECYCLE_SCRIPTS list and has the same sole purpose ("Generate version file after npm install (for CI)"), so it goes too.
- No *.local.json gitignore prompt. Gated on "will THIS run write a file" (mode + explicit --output), while hooks and lifecycle scripts are gated on the mode alone, since neither ever passes --output.
- No dynamic-version.local.d.ts: it is written by the same gated call.

OUTPUT HONESTY. VersionOutputData.outputPath is now string | null; null drops the "save" lines and the compact disk marker, so the CLI cannot report a save that did not happen. generateTypeDefinitions() now returns the .d.ts path it wrote, so that name is derived in one place instead of three.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE
- The watcher and the metro plugin still write the file in package-json mode: version-manager-70i.11, untouched here.
- Hooks/scripts left behind by an EARLIER install are not removed: version-manager-70i.6.
- A dynamic-version.local.json left behind by an earlier install is not removed either, and now goes stale: filed as version-manager-70i.15.
- bump still prints "Regenerating dynamic-version.local.json..." before calling the generate path, which in package-json mode now writes nothing. Left alone rather than reworded, because the line is shared with dynamic-file mode and this bead must not change dynamic-file output. Conductor's call.
- README/CLAUDE.md say nothing about any of this: version-manager-70i.12.
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. `bun run signal` clean. `bun test` with no failure main does not also have (baseline in the epic notes); run with npm_config_cache redirected into $TMPDIR or the install tests EPERM. New integration tests get an explicit per-test timeout of at least 20000ms.

BEHAVIOUR (each item needs a test)
1. In package-json mode, a hooked commit leaves NO dynamic-version.local.json and NO dynamic-version.local.d.ts anywhere in the repo, while package.json carries the bumped version.

title: Harden the merge driver command: a driver that cannot run loses their changes silently
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-19 while building 70i.8. When the command in `merge.version-manager.driver` cannot RUN at all, git reports `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in package.json` and marks the path UU — but the file left in the working tree is OURS verbatim, with NO conflict markers. An author who sees the conflict, opens the file, finds nothing to resolve and runs `git add package.json && git commit` SILENTLY DISCARDS the other side's package.json changes entirely (probe: their new dependency was simply gone).

This is the exact shape critical rule 6 exists to prevent: a failed measurement arriving as a calm, plausible result. It is a trap the driver INTRODUCES — without any driver, git writes conflict markers and the loss cannot happen.

HOW LIKELY. The registered command is `npx @justinhaaheim/version-manager merge-driver %O %A %B`. npx cannot resolve this GitHub-only package without node_modules, which is the same failure the hooks already carry `nonFatalSuffix` for. A `git worktree add` produces exactly that state and SHARES .git/config, so the driver is registered while node_modules is absent.

PINNED BY a test in tests/integration/merge-driver.test.ts ("a driver command that cannot RUN leaves a conflict with no markers (known trap)"), which uses `false` as the driver command. The README documents it under "Known limitations".
design:
FIX SHAPES CONSIDERED, none implemented — this is a design decision, not a typo.

A. WRAP THE COMMAND WITH A CHANGED-FILE GUARD (most robust found).
   `cp %A $tmp; <driver> %O %A %B; c=$?; if [ $c -ne 0 ] && cmp -s %A $tmp; then git merge-file %A %O %B; exit $?; fi; exit $c`
   Correct because our driver only ever writes %A through git merge-file: non-zero AND %A byte-identical to ours means the driver did nothing, so do the normal merge. Cost: a multi-command shell string with a temp file living in git config, which has failure modes of its own.

B. DISCRIMINATE ON EXIT CODE. Rejected, measured as unsound: npx failing to resolve the package exits 1, which is indistinguishable from "git merge-file found 1 conflict". The likeliest failure is exactly the one this cannot see.

C. REGISTER A DIRECT PATH instead of npx (node ./node_modules/.../dist/index.js). Narrows the window but does not close it — the same missing node_modules breaks it.

D. DOCUMENT ONLY. What 70i.8 shipped: a README "Known limitations" bullet telling the author not to stage a package.json conflict that contains no markers, plus the pinning test.

ALSO WORTH DECIDING HERE: whether the driver should be registered at all for a package installed from GitHub, given 70i.20 (committed dist/ is stale, so `npx` from GitHub would not even have the merge-driver subcommand).
acceptance_criteria: A merge whose driver command cannot run either (a) produces a normal conflict WITH markers, or (b) fails in a way that cannot be mistaken for a resolved file. A test drives the failing-command case and asserts the other side is not lost. The existing trap test is updated or replaced rather than left asserting the old behaviour.

title: No unregister path for the merge driver when versionMode changes
description:
Found while building 70i.8, same shape as 70i.6 (stale hooks) and deliberately not fixed there.

`install` in package-json mode registers the merge driver: it appends `package.json merge=version-manager` to .gitattributes (COMMITTED, so it travels to every clone and every branch) and sets merge.version-manager.driver/.name in .git/config. There is no path that takes either back.

CONSEQUENCES of switching versionMode from package-json to dynamic-file, or of dropping version-manager entirely:
- .gitattributes keeps pointing package.json at the driver, on every branch, forever.
- The git config entries stay, so deliberate version bumps in dynamic-file mode are now silently resolved to OURS on merge — the thing 70i.8 deliberately declined to install for that mode.
- A clone that never runs install just falls back to the built-in merge (measured, benign), so the committed attribute alone is harmless. The harm needs the config half.

NOT URGENT: nobody is in this state yet. Filed so it is visible rather than discovered.
design: FIX SHAPE: an unregister step that runs when install detects a versionMode that does not want the driver — remove the `[merge "version-manager"]` section with `git config --remove-section` (NOT --unset of one key: a .name with no .driver makes git abort every merge with `fatal: custom merge driver version-manager lacks command line`, measured 2026-09-19), and remove the .gitattributes line we added, leaving any other line in that file untouched. Best done together with 70i.6, which has the identical shape for hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Installing in package-json mode and then in dynamic-file mode leaves no merge.version-manager config section and no package.json merge= line that version-manager added; an unrelated .gitattributes line survives; a test drives both installs in one fixture repo and then proves a diverged merge conflicts normally (exit 1, markers present) rather than aborting.

title: Merge driver registration must be behind a knob, default off
description:
BUILT 2026-09-19 in commit 6db1038 on pr-4-package-json-mode. The merge driver from 70i.8 is merged and off by default; turning it on is an explicit, documented opt-in.

WHY THE KNOB EXISTS (unchanged, and the reason the default must stay off). The driver code is correct; INSTALLING it is what exposes a repository to the hazard measured in 70i.22. When the registered driver COMMAND cannot run, git reports 'CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in package.json', marks the path UU, and leaves the file as OURS VERBATIM WITH NO CONFLICT MARKERS. An author who sees a conflict, opens the file, finds nothing to resolve and runs 'git add package.json' SILENTLY DISCARDS the other side. Without any driver registered git writes markers and this cannot happen. The registered command is 'npx @justinhaaheim/version-manager ...', and 'git worktree add' produces exactly the state where that cannot resolve while sharing .git/config. Justin uses worktrees constantly. Justin's feature-knobs rule — merge the code early, off by default, behind a knob — is precisely for this.

WHAT LANDED
- src/types.ts: MergeDriverConfigSchema ({enabled: boolean, default false}, itself .default({enabled: false})), declared in VersionManagerConfigSchema, plus the MergeDriverConfig type. Same shape and defaulting style as branchSuffix.
- src/version-generator.ts: isMergeDriverEnabled(), mirroring getVersionMode(). Returns false when there is no config AND when the config could not be parsed — an unreadable config must never be the reason a repo ends up with a driver. Both config literals (getDefaultVersionManagerConfig, migrateLegacyConfig) now carry mergeDriver: {enabled: false}, so a freshly created or migrated version-manager.json writes the knob out explicitly, off.
- src/index.ts: installCommand registers the driver only when versionMode === 'package-json' AND isMergeDriverEnabled(). With the knob off install says nothing about merge drivers; with it on, every message and failure behaviour 70i.8 built is unchanged.
- tests/helpers/repo-fixtures.ts: MergeDriverFixtureConfig, an optional trailing parameter on setupPackageJsonModeRepo and setupRepoForInstall. Omitted, the fixture writes no mergeDriver key at all, which is what every existing project's config looks like.

DOCUMENTED in the README's 'The package.json merge driver' section (commit for 70i.12), which now opens with how to turn the knob on and why it is off.

STILL OUT OF SCOPE, and the knob does not fix either: hardening the driver command (70i.22) and unregistering on mode change (70i.23). The knob makes 70i.22 a considered opt-in rather than an ambush.
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. `bun run signal` clean; `TMPDIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" npm_config_cache="$TMPDIR/npm-cache" bun run test` with no failure main does not also have (the 8 in the epic notes).

BEHAVIOUR (each needs a test)
1. Default off: install in package-json mode with no mergeDriver field writes NO .gitattributes entry and NO merge.version-manager git config, and its output does not mention merge drivers.
2. Knob on: install in package-json mode with mergeDriver.enabled true registers both, exactly as the 70i.8 tests already assert.
3. Knob on but dynamic-file mode: nothing is registered. Both conditions are required.
4. The 70i.8 merge-behaviour tests still pass, with their fixtures opting the knob on.
5. A config carrying mergeDriver parses; one omitting it parses and defaults to off.

NEGATIVE CONTROL (required, and reported): remove the knob from the condition, watch test 1 fail, restore it, report the failure message.
notes:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, item by item.
1. Default off. tests/integration/merge-driver.test.ts, 'DEFAULT OFF: package-json mode with no mergeDriver field registers nothing and says nothing'. Runs a NON-silent install (the point is what a watching user is told) and asserts: exit 0, no .gitattributes file, merge.version-manager.driver unset, merge.version-manager.name unset, and neither stdout nor stderr matching /merge[ -]?driver/i, 'merge=version-manager' or '.gitattributes'. PASSES.
2. Knob on. 'KNOB ON: package-json mode with mergeDriver.enabled registers both halves' asserts the .gitattributes line, the driver command containing 'merge-driver %O %A %B', a non-empty .name, and that install now DOES mention it. The four AC5 install tests and every merge test in the file also opt the knob on and are unchanged otherwise. PASSES.
3. Both conditions. 'BOTH CONDITIONS: the knob on in dynamic-file mode still registers nothing' — the mode veto is independent of the knob. PASSES.
4. The 70i.8 merge tests still pass with their fixtures opting in: 15 pass / 0 fail in tests/integration/merge-driver.test.ts (12 pre-existing + 3 new).
5. Schema. Four unit tests in tests/unit/merge-driver.test.ts: a config omitting mergeDriver parses and defaults to off; one carrying it keeps the value; an empty object defaults to off; a non-boolean 'enabled' is REJECTED rather than coerced to on.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, run and recorded. With '&& isMergeDriverEnabled()' removed from the condition in installCommand, the default-off test fails on exactly the right assertion, and on the first one that can discriminate:
  568 | expect(repo.fileExists('.gitattributes')).toBe(false);
  error: expect(received).toBe(expected)
  Expected: false
  Received: true
Restored, and the file is 15/15 again. Note the 'BOTH CONDITIONS' test does NOT fail under that control, correctly: it isolates the mode half, which the control leaves in place.

DECISIONS WORTH KNOWING
- isMergeDriverEnabled() re-reads version-manager.json rather than threading the parsed config through installCommand, exactly as getVersionMode() already does. Two reads per install; mirroring the existing pattern was judged better than a one-off refactor in a knob dispatch. Same shape as 70i.19's complaint about the pre-commit path, so if that is ever fixed, fix this with it.
- A freshly created version-manager.json now contains "mergeDriver": {"enabled": false}. That is deliberate: the knob is discoverable in the file rather than only in the README. No test asserted the default config's exact bytes, and the 'does not rewrite a config already in the new format' migration test still passes because a config without the key parses without migrating.

Conductor confirmed this repo itself has no .gitattributes and no merge.version-manager git config, so nothing leaked into the checkout the work was done in. Negative control run and reported. title: PROPOSAL: timestamp in a dedicated committed file, not a count in package.json
description:
Justin, 2026-09-19, restating the goal after five dispatches of building package-json mode: "The important thing about this repo is not the exact implementation. It's having a seamless and easy-to-use tool that makes versioning projects simpler, and that doesn't require a human/agent to be constantly needing to remember to bump a version number... can we automatically generate a version number that has similar qualities to the commit hash, but that is easily understandable to everyone and conveys meaningful information about the code being different?... can we make versioning automatic, simple, and not prone to errors/footguns?" He named ~/Dev/prompts as the target shape: a library, no runtime version, no React Native, no OTA.

THE DIAGNOSIS. Every footgun this epic measured traces to ONE design choice, and it is not the pre-commit hook. It is that the committed version encodes a COUNT. A count is a claim about history, so it has to stay true as history is rewritten, and the hook does not fire on the operations that rewrite it. Measured, all of them:
- git commit --amend re-runs pre-commit and double-bumps.
- git rebase never re-runs the hook: commits accrue, the version stands still.
- git merge fires pre-merge-commit, not pre-commit, so auto-merge commits keep a stale count.
- Two branches of equal length compute the SAME count, so git auto-merges the line and the result undercounts.
- Unequal branches always conflict on package.json.
- The merge driver that fixes the conflicts introduces a data-loss trap (70i.22): when its command cannot run, git reports a conflict but leaves the file as ours with NO markers, so `git add` silently discards the other side.
None of those exist for a value that makes no claim about history.

THE PROPOSAL — three changes, each deleting a category rather than adding a guard.

1. PAYLOAD: a timestamp instead of a count. This repo already computes exactly the right string (generateBuildNumber(), iOS-compatible YYYYMMDD.HHMMSS.SS). It is monotonic, globally unique across branches with no coordination, ordered so you can always tell which of two builds is newer, and it answers the question Justin actually asks of a screenshot, which is WHEN, not HOW FAR PAST 0.3.0. Amend just gets a new timestamp, which is correct. Rebase leaves the old one, which is stale but never WRONG. Two branches can never collide.

2. LOCATION: a dedicated committed file (version.json or version.txt), not package.json's version field. package.json's version goes back to being an ordinary human-bumped semver that npm and the ecosystem understand. This deletes the whole semver-compatibility layer built in this epic: prerelease ownership (D3), npm stripping +N build metadata (70i.1), sanitising a branch name into a legal prerelease identifier, and most of the reason the pre-commit write had to be surgical at all.

3. MERGE: git's own built-in trivial driver instead of a custom command. VERIFIED BY EXPERIMENT 2026-09-19 in a throwaway repo, not assumed: with `version.txt merge=vm-ours` in .gitattributes and `merge.vm-ours.driver = true` in git config, a merge where BOTH sides changed version.txt AND the feature side added a dependency to package.json completed with exit 0, kept ours for version.txt, and kept the feature's dependency in package.json. `true` is a shell builtin, so unlike `npx @justinhaaheim/version-manager` it CANNOT fail to resolve — which is the single condition that triggers 70i.22's data loss. This fix is only available once the version lives alone in its own file: pointing `driver = true` at package.json would discard the other side's real changes every time.

WHAT IS KEPT. The pre-commit hook, and the index-aware surgical write built in 70i.3 (a value inside the commit has to be written to the index mid-commit; that part is right and tested). The fail-loudly contract from 70i.4. The branch suffix from 70i.10, which becomes a nice-to-have for identification rather than load-bearing for collision avoidance.

WHAT IS LOST, honestly. "0.3.5 means five commits past 0.3.0" goes away. A timestamp says when, not how much. Justin liked add-to-patch; this is the one thing he would be giving up, and it is the same thing that causes every footgun above, so it cannot be kept AND fixed.

WHAT BECOMES MOOT IF THIS LANDS: 70i.22 (harden the driver command), 70i.23 (no unregister path), most of 70i.8, and the semver half of 70i.10. 70i.20 (stale committed dist) still matters and matters MORE, since a stale dist is what makes the registered command missing.

STATUS: a proposal, not a decision. Justin invited it; he has not chosen it.

title: Pre-commit hook must read the INDEX, not the working tree
description:
DONE on branch pr-4-package-json-mode (commits e7987a8, df89647). Awaiting conductor review; NOT closed by the player.

THE BUG (fixed). The pre-commit hook read the WORKING TREE package.json, rewrote its version, then ran `git add package.json` on the whole file. Any unstaged edit sitting in package.json — a half-added dependency, a script being drafted — was silently swept into a commit the author never staged it for. That puts content into history the author did not choose to commit.

WHAT NOW EXISTS (epic design D9)
- The base version is read from the INDEX. When package.json is unstaged the index holds HEAD's content, so one rule covers the staged and the unstaged case with no branching, and an unstaged VERSION edit can no longer steer the calculation.
- The new index content is the index content with only the version value replaced, written with `git hash-object -w --stdin` + `git update-index --cacheinfo`. Nothing else about the index moves. package.json is no longer passed to `git add` — that would undo exactly this.
- The working-tree file gets a string-level replacement of the same value, never a parse-and-re-stringify.
- package.json absent from the index falls back to the working tree, warns, and writes the WORKING TREE ONLY. Interpretation of D9, which specifies only the read fallback: adding a whole unstaged file to the index would be the larger version of the bug being fixed.

CODE
- src/json-text-edit.ts (NEW): findTopLevelStringValueSpan / replaceTopLevelStringValue. A depth-tracking scanner, because "version" is not unique in a package.json (nested in overrides/volta, and a dependency literally named `version` exists on npm). 13 unit tests in tests/unit/json-text-edit.test.ts.
- src/git-utils.ts: readIndexEntry() / writeIndexEntry(). Sync + execFileSync, NOT the module's async execCommand(), because the write needs stdin, the callers are sync, and execCommand() .trim()s its output — which would eat package.json's trailing newline.
- src/script-manager.ts: readPreCommitBaseVersion() / writePreCommitVersion() bodies replaced.
- src/version-generator.ts: consumes the richer read; new GenerateVersionResult.preCommitBaseWarning.
- src/index.ts: preCommitHandler no longer stages package.json; prints the fallback warning.

MEASURED FACTS worth not rediscovering
- `git update-index --cacheinfo` resolves its path from the REPO ROOT while `git ls-files -- <path>` matches relative to CWD. Run from a subdirectory, a bare 'package.json' silently overwrites the ROOT package.json's index entry. That is why the path comes from `git ls-files --full-name`.
- `git commit -a`: git stages tracked modifications into the real index before pre-commit runs, so the hook reads them and the result is correct.
- Partial commits (`git commit -- <path>`): the hook runs against a TEMPORARY index, so the surgical write lands in the commit correctly (the unstaged edit stays out), but the REAL index keeps the pre-commit version and `git status` shows `MM package.json`. MEASURED to be pre-existing: the same probe against the pre-change code (0ef1f60) showed the identical stale real index, plus the unstaged edit in HEAD. Filed separately.

SHAPE DEVIATIONS from the bead text, all deliberate and reported
1. The git-utils helper returns GitIndexEntry|null (content + mode + repo-relative path), not string|null: the mode and path are needed for a correct write and must come from the SAME measurement (critical rule 6.2, "one nullable field, not many"). Null still means strictly "not in the index".
2. readPreCommitBaseVersion() returns {source, version}|null rather than string|null, so D9's "say so in verbose output" can travel to the CLI the way branchSuffixWarning already does.

OUT OF SCOPE AND UNTOUCHED: 70i.4 (fail loudly on a failed stage), 70i.8 (amend/rebase/merge), 70i.5 (drop updateLockfile).
